questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Cuba?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Cuba article.

questions.proof: Havana is the capital city of Cuba.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Cuba?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Cuba on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Cuba article.

questions.proof: Cuba is near the United States, Mexico, Haiti, Jamaica and the Bahamas.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Cuba?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Cuba article.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The second largest city is _____ de Cuba.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “city”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Cuba article.

questions.proof: The second largest city is Santiago de Cuba.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In April _____, historic talks took place with US president Barack Obama and Cuban first secretary Raúl Castro about improving relations between the two nations.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Cuban Revolution” part of the Cuba article.

questions.proof: In April 2015, historic talks took place with US president Barack Obama and Cuban first secretary Raúl Castro about improving relations between the two nations.
